items.title: Curtis Mitchell Interview, 1996-04-02
items.q: He said, man, I need a bass player, man. I got a job at the Texas Lounge... I said, why don't you come on and make the gig?

ctx.x: See I was. Yeah. Because it seemed like most of the, yeah. In fact I'm surprised you, all these other instruments because I know you was a bass player. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Well piano was my first

Well anyway, I started playing bass. I was standing in the doodrop and I didn't have no job, you know. And the telephone rang in there and the bartender said, telephone for you. So I gets the phone and there's Raymond Montrell, Roy Montrell. He said, man, I need a bass player, man. I got a job at the Texas Lounge. The Texas Lounge was on Canal Street. Brass Rail was in the next block. He said, I got a job six nights a week. I need a bass player. You know I can find one? I said, no, man. He said, man, I can try…
